title: Spherical bots with uniform cilia may not move because ciliary forces cancel

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Spherical bots with uniform cilia may not move because ciliary forces cancel

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Morphotype 1 Anthrobots are likely non-movers or stationary wigglers, which the authors suggest may be because their radially symmetric spherical shape with evenly distributed cilia makes ciliary propulsion forces cancel out, with small imbalances producing only wiggling.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Distinct Movement Types and Morphotypes are Highly Correlated

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: This may be attributable to their spherical shape with homogeneously distributed cilia where the propulsion forces generated by the ciliary motion are more prone to canceling each other out due to the radially symmetric spherical shape, resulting in little or no movement.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Gumuskaya G, Srivastava P, Cooper BG, Lesser H, Semegran B, Garnier S, Levin M, “Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells”, Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) (2024), doi:10.1002/advs.202303575; section “Results › Distinct Movement Types and Morphotypes are Highly Correlated”. Scope: Small, spherical, uniformly ciliated Anthrobots (morphotype 1)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-anthrobots-15: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.56

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Force cancellation has a clear biomechanical test, but existing morphology-motion correlations do not measure the required forces. New ciliary-flow or force data are needed to distinguish the mechanism.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate ciliary force vectors from beat orientation and frequency, predict net thrust for each bot, and test whether symmetric morphotype-1 bots have near-zero vector sums and only residual wiggling.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Cilia distribution images do not provide force direction and magnitude.

Shape, adhesion, and orientation offer rival explanations for nonmovement.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.48
discriminating power: 0.58
operationalizability: 0.82
data adequacy: 0.35
analysis feasibility: 0.62

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Force cancellation is a quantitative mechanics claim about the cilia actually on small spherical bots. Neither the masks nor the beat directions are public, so the vector sum cannot be run. Symmetry plus little movement is compatible with several causes, and separating them needs the missing geometry or a new perturbation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: From real morphotype-1 cilia positions and beat directions, sum the propulsion vectors and compare the residual to measured displacement; alternatively, break the radial symmetry and ask whether wigglers start to translate. Near-zero net force on non-movers, and translation after symmetry is broken, would support cancellation; large residuals on bots that still do not move, or translation despite symmetric cilia, would point to another cause.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
An idealized sphere simulation would not be a test of these bots.

Immobility is also explained by weak beat, adhesion or substrate friction.

Cilia coordinates and beat directions for morphotype 1 are not deposited.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.32
data existence: 0.12
data adequacy: 0.12
analysis feasibility: 0.25
operationalizability: 0.6
